answer.raw_answer:
## Summary
There is no record of a "municipal library" opening at Vostok Station in 2019, nor does the station function as a public facility capable of hosting such an event. Vostok Station is a remote, highly restricted Russian scientific research outpost, and the concept of a "municipal" opening day with visitors is inconsistent with the station's operational reality.

## Operational Reality of Vostok Station
<details>
<summary>Analysis of station facilities and accessibility</summary>

Vostok Station is a remote Russian research facility located in inland Antarctica, primarily dedicated to scientific monitoring, including meteorology, aerology, geophysics, and ice core research [Source 1 — meduza.io](https://meduza.io/en/feature/2020/12/22/trouble-at-the-vostok-station), [Source 9 — meduza.io](https://meduza.io/en/feature/2020/12/22/trouble-at-the-vostok-station). It is not a public facility, and it does not have "municipal" infrastructure or a tourist season [Source 6 — wildexpedition.com](https://wildexpedition.com/province/vostok-station-east-antarctica-coldest-place-on-earth), [Source 7 — wildexpedition.com](https://wildexpedition.com/province/vostok-station-east-antarctica-coldest-place-on-earth).

The station's population is limited to scientific and support personnel, typically numbering 25–30 during the summer and 12–13 during the winter [Source 6 — wildexpedition.com](https://wildexpedition.com/province/vostok-station-east-antarctica-coldest-place-on-earth), [Source 9 — meduza.io](https://meduza.io/en/feature/2020/12/22/trouble-at-the-vostok-station). Access is strictly restricted to authorized scientific and logistical personnel, and there are no public roads or transportation options to the station [Source 7 — wildexpedition.com](https://wildexpedition.com/province/vostok-station-east-antarctica-coldest-place-on-earth), [Source 10 — wildexpedition.com](https://wildexpedition.com/province/vostok-station-east-antarctica-coldest-place-on-earth).

</details>

## Context Regarding 2019 Developments
<details>
<summary>Review of 2019 station activities</summary>

While there is no evidence of a library opening in 2019, the year was significant for the station's infrastructure planning. In 2019, the Russian government signed a decree to build an entirely new wintering complex at Vostok Station, following years of the existing facility falling into disrepair [Source 1 — meduza.io](https://meduza.io/en/feature/2020/12/22/trouble-at-the-vostok-station), [Source 4 — meduza.io](https://meduza.io/en/feature/2020/12/22/trouble-at-the-vostok-station). Additionally, in May 2019, officials announced plans to upgrade Vostok Station to increase its capacity to house up to 35 people in non-winter seasons [Source 3 — www.xinhuanet.com](https://www.xinhuanet.com/english/2019-05/24/c_138083964.htm).

Regarding the term "library," search results mention an "ice core library" inaugurated by the Ice Memory Foundation; however, this facility is distinct from a municipal library and was opened in January 2026, not 2019 [Source 14 — seas.umich.edu](https://seas.umich.edu/news/inaugurated-antarcticas-first-ice-core-library).

</details>

## Key Takeaways
*   **No Municipal Library:** There is no evidence of a municipal library at Vostok Station.
*   **Restricted Access:** Vostok Station is a scientific research base, not a public venue; it does not host "visitors" or public opening events.
*   **2019 Context:** The year 2019 was marked by government decrees to rebuild the station's aging wintering complex, rather than the inauguration of public facilities.
*   **Terminology Confusion:** The concept of an "ice core library" exists in Antarctic research, but it is a scientific archive, not a public library, and was inaugurated in 2026.
